cases.notes: Proves the ignored directory is pruned during the walk (never descended into), not filtered from a full listing afterward — see walk()'s is_path_ignored check on a trailing-slash-suffixed probe path, the implementation.

Default SearchOptions is case-insensitive (case_sensitive: false), matching 'answer' in 'const answer = 42;' (src/app.ts:1) and '// the ANSWER helper' (src/util.ts:1). debug.log is gitignored so it's never read.
With case_sensitive true, 'ANSWER' matches only the literal-uppercase occurrence in src/util.ts's comment; src/app.ts's lowercase 'answer' does not match.
max_results = 1 caps the result set below the true match count and sets truncated: true rather than silently returning a partial list with no signal.

Without whole_word, 'set' matches both the standalone identifier on line 1 and the substring inside 'offset' on line 2. With whole_word: true, the matcher is wrapped \b(?:set)\b, so only line 1 matches.

The pattern is the literal raw string r"fn \w+\(". With regex: true it's compiled as a pattern and matches both function declarations. With regex: false (default) the same text is escaped and searched for literally, matching nothing since no line contains that exact backslash-laden substring.

An unbalanced '(' fails Regex::new; build_matcher reduces the regex engine's multi-line Display error to its last line, trimmed, and prefixes 'invalid regular expression: '. The exact suffix text is not asserted by the original test (only the prefix is), so only the prefix is a binding contract.

A bare pattern with no '/' (e.g. '*.ts') is rewritten to '**/*.ts' and matches by file name at any depth; a pattern with '/' (e.g. 'docs/**') is matched against the full repo-relative path. Result order follows the walk's file_name()-sorted traversal: 'src/a.test.ts' sorts before 'src/a.ts' lexicographically ('e' < 's' at the 4th character). Exclude is applied after, and independent of, include — it can only remove, never re-admit., build_globs at the implementation.

src/b.ts has no match so it is never touched (files: 1, not 2). The checkpoint is taken before any file is written via the checkpoint helpernt::create(repo_path, "replace-all") — that mechanism's internals are owned by the git-checkpoint domain document, not this one; here it is exercised as an opaque dependency whose restore() reverts the write.

only_path scopes the walk's candidate list to exactly 'a.ts' before any matching happens, so b.ts is never even read despite also matching the pattern. $1/$2 capture-group references in the replacement string work because options.regex is true, using the regex engine's replace_all group-reference syntax.
